subtitle: Technological Progress, Sustainable Convergence and Long-Term Resilience

contribution: Establishes a rigorous, academically oriented synthesis within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series—concept developed by Hunter Hughes—integrating seven research pillars to chart humanity's long-term trajectory under compounding global risks through 2100.
keywords: The Future of Humanity Under Compounding Global Risks
abstract: The Future of Humanity Under Compounding Global Risks is a flagship publication within the H Heuristics Polycrisis Resilience Series, based on the concept developed by Hunter Hughes, Founder of H Heuristics (https://polycrisisresilience.hheuristics.com/).

keyFindings.title: Humanity's long-term future under compounding global risks is shaped by non-linear interactions across climate, pollution, infrastructure, demographics, and geopolitics—where unmitigated drift pushes global risk from 64.0 (2025) to 92.0 by 2100.
Synchronizing technological progress, sustainable economic convergence, and structural resilience across all seven research pillars compresses global compounding risk to 11.0 by 2100 (-82.8%).
Proactive resilience investments yield 9.5x–11.4x social benefit-cost ratios over 25 years, compared with 1.5x for reactive fragmented crisis relief.
Under Resilient Convergence, Global South real GDP per capita rises from 24.0% to 83.0% of the OECD frontier by 2100 while population exposed to high climate-pollution stress falls from 3.4B to 0.5B.
